html:
The Lombard kingdom of northern Italy and its semi-independent duchies further south, as the map shows them in 600 and 700. Between them lay lands still held by Byzantium.

The Lombards, a Germanic people, came from Pannonia in 568 under King Alboin, only fifteen years after Byzantium had finished the long Gothic War. They took most of the Po valley, still called Lombardy, and made Pavia their capital. Lombard dukes went further south and set up the duchies of Spoleto and Benevento, ruled almost as separate states. Byzantium kept Ravenna, Rome, Naples and the far south.

Over time the Lombards became Catholics and wrote down their laws in Latin, starting with the Edict of Rothari in 643. In 751 King Aistulf took Ravenna. The popes, fearing for Rome, called in the Franks, and in 774 Charlemagne conquered the kingdom for the Frankish realm. The Papal States grew from lands he confirmed to the popes. Benevento lasted as a Lombard principality until the 11th century; the later map shape is Lombard duchies.
sum: The Lombard kingdom of northern Italy and its semi-independent duchies further south, as the map shows them in 600 and 700. Between them lay lands still held by Byzantium.
